title: "The app, and publishing"
---



Two stages are left: an explorer so that people can interrogate the estimates
themselves, and the command that puts this book on the web.

## Anatomy of a Shiny app

Every Shiny app is three objects and one idea.

| Piece | What it is | In this app |
|---|---|---|
| `ui` | a nested list of HTML widgets | `fluidPage(sidebarLayout(...))` |
| `server` | a function of `input`, `output`, `session` | computes the estimates, draws the plot |
| `shinyApp(ui, server)` | wires them together and serves them | the last line of the file |

The idea is **reactivity**. You never write "when the user clicks, recompute." You
declare what each output *is*, in terms of inputs, and Shiny works out what to re-run
when something changes.

::: {.pipeline}
::: {.stage}
[input$by]{.name}

[the control]{.sub}
:::
::: {.stage}
[est()]{.name}

[reactive]{.sub}
:::
::: {.stage}
[output$plot]{.name}

[render]{.sub}
:::
:::

Three kinds of object in that chain, and the distinction is the whole framework:

- **`input$x`** — read-only, set by the browser. Touching `input$state` anywhere makes
  that code depend on it.
- **`reactive({ ... })`** — a computation that **caches** and re-runs only when
  something it read has changed. `est()` is called by both the plot and the table, and
  runs once.
- **`render*({ ... })`** — an output. It re-runs when a dependency changes and writes
  into `output$plot`.

::: {.warn}
[The two mistakes agents make here]{.warn-head}
Asking for a reactive's value outside a reactive context (`est()` at the top level —
"operation not allowed without an active reactive context"), and recomputing the same
summary separately in each `render*` block instead of sharing one `reactive()`. The
second one is not an error; it is just the app doing the work twice.
:::

### This app, line by line


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```
#> library(shiny)
#> library(tidyverse)
#> source(here::here("R/functions.R"))
#> 
#> wss <- read_rds(here::here("data/wss_clean.rds"))
#> 
#> ui <- fluidPage(
#>   titlePanel("Western States Survey: Trump vote, 2020 vs 2024"),
#>   sidebarLayout(
#>     sidebarPanel(
#>       checkboxGroupInput("state", "State", sort(unique(wss$state)), sort(unique(wss$state))),
#>       selectInput("by", "Compare by", c("latino", "race4", "auth_group", "age_group", "party3")),
#>       checkboxInput("wt", "Use survey weights", TRUE)
#>     ),
#>     mainPanel(plotOutput("plot"), tableOutput("tab"))
#>   )
#> )
#> 
#> server <- function(input, output, session) {
#>   est <- reactive({
#>     wss |>
#>       filter(state %in% input$state) |>
#>       trump_share(input$by, weighted = input$wt)
#>   })
#>   output$plot <- renderPlot(
#>     ggplot(est(), aes(year, trump, colour = .data[[input$by]], group = .data[[input$by]])) +
#>       geom_point(size = 3) + geom_line() +
#>       scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
#>       labs(x = NULL, y = "Two-party Trump share", colour = NULL) +
#>       theme_minimal(base_size = 15)
#>   )
#>   output$tab <- renderTable(est())
#> }
#> 
#> shinyApp(ui, server)
```
:::


```bash
Rscript -e 'shiny::runApp("app")'
```

Read it top to bottom:

1. **Load once, outside `server`.** Code above `ui` runs a single time when the app
   starts, not per user and not per click. The data read belongs there.
2. **`source("R/functions.R")`.** The app calls `trump_share()` — the same function
   the analysis script calls. The app holds *no* analysis logic of its own, so it
   cannot drift away from the paper.
3. **The UI names the inputs.** `inputId = "by"` in the UI is `input$by` in the server.
   That string is the entire contract between the two halves.
4. **`.data[[input$by]]`** — the tidy-evaluation form for a column chosen at runtime.
   An agent will often write `get(input$by)` or paste strings together; both work until
   they don't.
5. **A weights toggle.** Making "weighted or not" visible in the interface is honest,
   and it shows the audience how much the weighting is doing.
6. **`n_obs` and `n_miss` in the table.** Every point in the plot has a sample size
   behind it, and some of them are small.

### Why it is testable

`server` is an ordinary R function, so it can be run without a browser —
`shiny::testServer()` sets inputs and reads the reactives back. That is what
[the app's integration tests](09-tests.qmd) do. Two habits make an app testable at all:
keep the computation in a named function outside the app, and keep the `server` body
thin enough to read.

::: {.warn}
[What this app would need before anyone else used it]{.warn-head}
Cell-size suppression, for one — a filtered panel can easily land on fewer than 30
respondents, and a point estimate drawn from them invites exactly the over-reading this
project is about. Intervals, too; the plot shows points with no uncertainty at all.
:::

## Publishing

The site, the book, and the slides are one Quarto project:

```bash
quarto render                 # build everything into _site/
quarto preview                # live reload while writing
quarto publish gh-pages       # render, then push to the gh-pages branch
```

`quarto publish gh-pages` commits the rendered output to a `gh-pages` branch and leaves
your source branch alone. GitHub Pages serves it at
[crweber9874.github.io/UNM_Workshop](https://crweber9874.github.io/UNM_Workshop/).

### Freeze, and why it is committed

```yaml
execute:
  freeze: auto
```

Chapters that run R store their results in `_freeze/`. A rebuild re-runs only what
changed, which keeps the render fast and means the book can be rebuilt on a machine
without the data. Delete `_freeze/` and render again when you want to prove the whole
thing still reproduces.

### What is deliberately not committed


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}


|Not committed      |Why                                                |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------|
|data/wss_clean.rds |regenerate it: Rscript R/01_recode.R               |
|output/            |figures and tables are rebuilt by R/02_analysis.R  |
|_site/             |rendered output; gh-pages holds the published copy |
|.Renviron, .env    |secrets never belong in a repository               |
|raw .dta files     |not ours to distribute                             |


:::
:::


The principle: commit the **instructions** for producing a thing, not the thing — unless
the thing is expensive to produce and cheap to store, which is the argument for
`_freeze/`.

## The whole pipeline, one command at a time

```bash
Rscript R/01_recode.R                              # csv  -> data/wss_clean.rds
Rscript R/02_analysis.R                            # models, figures -> output/
Rscript -e 'testthat::test_dir("tests/testthat")'  # checks pass?
Rscript -e 'shiny::runApp("app")'                  # explore
quarto render                                      # book + slides -> _site/
quarto publish gh-pages                            # publish
```

Six commands, one direction, no step that depends on something a person remembered to do
by hand. That is the standard an agent has to be held to as well — [and how you hold it
there](11-verification.qmd) is the last chapter.
